assumptions: SOL column = public VR200 spec peaks (BF16 4 / FP8 17.5 / FP4 35 PF dense, HBM4 22 TB/s, NVLink6 1.8 TB/s per direction), zero per-kernel gap; there is no public NVLink latency figure, so a dependent hop uses our measured one-way flag (2.86 us) and is never set below a measured hand-off. Achievable column = our Hecate measurements (3.65 / 10.9 / 21.1 PF, 13.9 TB/s, 2.86 us push hop + 0.035 us per polled peer, 0.78 us graph node) plus the wave-1 microbench fixes (2026-11-18): push 1.06 TB/s (measured ceiling), NVLS AR alpha 12.6-12.9 us + algbw 0.64/0.77/0.84/0.88 TB/s (N = 2/4/8/16, multimem kernel), NVLS RS alpha + M / 1.06 TB/s (0.88 at N = 2), standalone exchange floor = fastest measured exchange per N (3.86/4.22/4.49/4.89 us; fused sdec TP-path exchanges pay the hop only), 2 us floor on the grid-dependent kernels (KDA recurrence, indexer, sparse MLA, MegaMoE), MegaMoE expert weights streamed die-local (17.1 TB/s). Tests keep the column at or below every comm / MegaMoE / step row and e2e anchor. No fitted derating; the calibrated column (calibrate.py) is the only derated one.
FP32 SIMT (131.6 TF) and MUFU exp (8.2 T/s) rates are derived from measured attributes (212 SMs x 128 lanes x 2, x 16 MUFU, x 2.424 GHz) in both columns (not measured).

Per-op roofline t = max(FLOPs/peak[dtype], bytes/HBM, SIMT/peak_simt + SFU/peak_mufu); ops are additive (no cross-op overlap) except two-microbatch O1. A launched (non-fused) kernel costs max(roofline, per-kernel gap): the gap overlaps the previous kernel under PDL; comm events pay their hop latency only.

Sparse MLA runs FP8 Q x FP8 KV MMAs (the 576-B per-tensor FP8 row; a 656-B fp8_ds_mla row would be BF16), co-bound with one MUFU exp per (row, head, key). The indexer is max(FP4 MMA, FP32 epilogue relu + head-weight FMA over 32 heads at the SIMT rate, key bytes).

Ops flagged fused_in_sol (conv, gate/beta norm, o_norm, act, gate_mul, top-k of MoE, latent_norm, ...) carry no activation HBM traffic, but their second input is read by the consumer (KDA / DSA o_proj read the output gate). The MoE fc1->fc2 intermediate stays in L2 up to 64 MiB per GPU (decode) and round-trips HBM above (prefill). O7 SOL fusions are always on: exact top-k without a full logits pass when cheaper (min of BF16 scratch write+read and a two-pass recompute; the scratch wins everywhere today), final AttnRes mix on the R logit rows and aux captures / drafter context rows only for consumed rows in prefill, Markov vocab shard reused from L2 (<= 64 MiB).

FP8 MLA KV is the standard 576-B row (512 latent + 64 rope FP8); MXFP4 indexer key 68 B; DSA KV = 15,456 B/token. Sparse-MLA KV reads use one SOL rule in both phases: the union bound min(Lu, Ltk) (decode: q x 2048 rows per request at 135K; the true union of overlapping verify rows is smaller, worth ~2% of a high-r DEP step).

KDA state per request = one FP32 recurrent state (434 MB) + FP32 conv (3+k columns) + RecoverSSM records (1024 B per row per head = 6.78 MB x q, written for q rows and read for AL rows per step; one constant drives traffic and capacity); the deployed allocator reserves far more (workload.md) - that gap is an implementation item.

mxfp4_release routed experts run W4A8 at the FP8 MMA rate with MXFP8 dispatch (3696 B/route); O4 (NVFP4 activations, FP4 rate, 2016 B/route) is not in the headline because the mission fixes MXFP8 activations. The deployed Rubin MegaMoE switches to NVFP4 above 512 tokens/rank: prefill microbenches must pin MXFP8 or compare to O4.

nvfp4_modelopt: experts NVFP4 W4A4 at FP4 rate (2016 B/route), KDA projections + shared experts MXFP8 at FP8 rate; MLA, router, latent, dense L0, lm_head BF16. KV/state precision identical to mxfp4_release.

Routing is uniform: experts touched per GPU = ceil(896/E) x (1 - (1 - 16/896)^(rows in EP domain)); EP sizes that do not divide 896 (72, 24) hold ceil(896/E) expert slots per GPU with redundant replicas carrying the load evenly (weights charged, imbalance 1.0 in both columns; O5 is a sensitivity knob, not applied).

All-reduce / reduce-scatter take the cheapest implemented primitive per column: NVLS multimem, one-shot Lamport push (1 hop, (N-1)M in) or two-shot push (2 hops). sdec-style Lamport pushes are priced at the flag hop (16-rank two-shot owner reduce measured 3.39 us after the last push); the torch one_shot (pull + barrier) bench does not apply to them.

TP-sharded MoE-dense (D7, D8, D10, D11): router/latent_down column shards are transposed to row ownership for top-k + dispatch, and the combined latent is transposed back for a K-split latent_up whose partials ride the shared-expert RS / AR (2 transposes per MoE layer; no replicated latent_up weights).

Async comm (ShardQ context push on the copy engine) hides under the attention compute of the same layer; all other comm is exposed unless O1 (two microbatches, t_layer = max(compute, comm), weights streamed twice) is on. ShardQ prefill uses slice-local q_b / W_UK / g with all-head weights (no q scatter) and an out gather before the head-TP o_proj.

DcpExchange top-k merge bytes 1536 B per row per peer (inferred); sharded verify 100 B per row per peer. DSA-DP decode push_in/out move 0 bytes (SP shards hold whole requests, the holder is the owner); prefill pays (N-1)/N.

Capacity: HBM budget 272.48 GiB (measured free at vLLM start) - resident weights - 16 GiB reserve (activations, graphs, symmetric buffers, MegaMoE arena). r_max is per GPU (a group of N holds N x r requests). SOL = byte-exact state; achievable = the packed hybrid block pool at the best pinnable block size (multiples of 64): whole bs-token rows of all 24 DSA layers per request (DSA rows ceil((L+1+k)/(bs x DCP)), G >= 3 KDA state groups x (1 + k) spec slots, drafter SWA ring; deployed D1 24 / 36 and D2 36 / 52 rows reproduced); the SP path is charged the byte-exact state (its measured 13 rows are not G x (1 + k) state rows).

MegaMoE (EP) is one persistent kernel: layer = max(expert ops, dispatch + combine bytes / NVLink) + combine drain hop + one expert's worth of the shorter phase (moe lane: the fused kernel hides the link under the GEMMs).

P1-type TP prefill: o_proj reduce-scatters in the GEMM, AttnRes runs on the 1/N token shard, a push AG rebuilds the rows (RS + AG per sublayer instead of an AR); TP decode (sdec) keeps the fused AR and all-row AttnRes.

Prefill chunks are packed from AgentX requests with 5,456 fresh tokens each over a 72.9K prefix (fresh-weighted mean); L_ref = 78.4K. Headline = best chunk size per engine in {4K..64K} that fits HBM (0.5 MB per row of live activations assumed). KDA state checkpoint export for the prefix cache is counted (CKPT=1). KDA core prefill has a chunk-serial latency floor (FlashKDA K2: ~0.49 us per 16-token chunk, kda_segscan.py) relieved by segment-parallel scan (3x K2 work + scan) - it matters for TTFT and few-sequence chunks only.

Decode reference context 135K (mission); r_max also reported at the OSL-weighted 189K. AL = golden 3.08/3.81/4.16 at k=3/5/7. Draft = one parallel 5-layer pass on k query rows + k sequential Markov steps.
DSA-DP owner balance and DP lock-step padding are taken as perfect (SOL); D10 split indexer therefore only adds comm here - its value is under owner skew, which the SOL model does not price.

PP (P7) stages are balanced by a DP partition over the per-layer times; the boundary push carries the residual + AttnRes block state (1 + ceil(l/12) rows of 14,336 B per token). Fill/drain bubbles ignored (many chunks in flight).

AFD (D11): two microbatches ping-pong; per MoE layer max(A layer, F experts, A<->F transfer) per half batch, transfer = max(egress, ingress) per side (full duplex); best of the A:F splits 56:16 / 48:24 / 40:32 per r; one capacity function (kv.afd_capacity) reports r_max per split.

Anchors are sanity checks only (never fitted): D1 e2e (21 runs), C512 D3 decode (r = B/4 per DP4 rank), C512 P2 prefill (computed prompt tokens) and PR #20 (24-layer layout ratios); the page flags any anchor where the achievable column is slower than measured.
open_questions: MoE activations for mxfp4_release prefill: MXFP8 (headline) or NVFP4 (the Rubin backend above 512 tokens/rank)?

C512 P2 prefill slope: the model's marginal cost (achievable ~16.7 ms per 1K chunk tokens, SOL ~13.5) is steeper than the quoted 11 ms/1K lower-bound fit; no per-step prefill logs exist to rebuild the measured slope.
SOL per-hop latency: no public NVLink latency figure; both columns use our measured one-way flag (2.86 us).
Dispatch dedup with per-rank FP32 pre-combine (O2) changes the BF16 rounding order of the routed sum - acceptable as 'order may differ'?
KDA core precision: FlashKDA stages the FP32 state into BF16 MMAs in prefill; FP32/TF32 math would ~2x the prefill KDA core.
DcpExchange per-row bytes (X_topk) and the drafter forward row count per verify outcome are inferred, not read from kernels.
Rack-wide EP (D7/D8/P6) imbalance factor: SOL uses 1.0; which measured EPLB max/mean should the achievable column use?
KDA segment-scan context parallel for long prompts (P8) reorders the FP32 recurrence across ranks.
The FP32 SIMT rate and the MXFP4 GEMM rate are not measured on VR200; die-local 17.1 TB/s comes from a code docstring.
Spec values are NVIDIA's preliminary public figures and may change.
